1.why: Text is set in a plain, legible sans-serif typeface with comfortable line and block spacing, although letter spacing is left at the default rather than being expanded.

2.why: Across all five screens every instruction is short sentence-case text with no italics, no all-caps strings, and no dense paragraphs.

3.why: The single-column, mobile-width layout with full-width inputs and ample whitespace reads clearly, though the page is sparse with a largely empty Logs area.

4.why: Each screen carries only one or two short plain-language sentences, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code delivered to your verified mobile number.'

5.why: No field shows a placeholder, sample value, or formatted example for the email address, phone number, or verification code.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is a single sentence, so the user is never forced to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The six-digit code must be typed into a plain text field, and no screen presents a secret or recovery code with a copy affordance.

8.why: No QR code, deep link, or any equivalent alternative to manual entry appears at any step of the flow.

9.why: The inputs are bare fields with no visible autocomplete or one-time-code hints and no password-manager integration, leaving only generic browser heuristics.

10.why: A bold heading names the current step and a single blue button is the obvious primary action, but there is no progress indicator showing where the user sits in the overall enrolment flow.

11.why: Each screen requests exactly one main action (Continue or Verify identity), even though the first screen collects two fields before that action.

12.why: The Logs line 'Identity verification delivery was initiated' states what happened and the next screen explains what to enter, but after the failed attempt the system only says 'try again' without plainly stating the outcome.

13.why: The user can resubmit after the error with the entered code retained and no stated penalty, but there are no reveal/hide controls and no way to re-request the code.

14.why: The red message 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is blame-free but never states the actual problem (e.g. wrong or expired code) or how to fix it beyond retrying.

15.why: No countdown, session timer, or expiry notice appears on any screen so reading is untimed, although the actual validity window of the SMS code is never disclosed.
